_note: The persona: the mask (CW6 ¶800, CW7 ¶305, ¶246), the outer face and its functions (CW6 ¶801), the mask the collective psyche wears (CW7 ¶245) and the role the public attributes (CW18 ¶1334), and the dismantling that individuation requires (CW7 ¶505, CW6 ¶807). Quotations are placed by the corpus; nothing is typed.
line: Jung's statements on the persona: its definition (CW6), its description as a mask and as a compromise between individual and society (CW7), the mask worn by the collective psyche, and the dissolution of the persona.

sections.title: The mask
sections.line: CW6 ¶800 (Definitions, 1921), CW7 ¶305 and ¶246: the name from the masks of actors in antiquity, and Jung's descriptions of the persona as a kind of mask and as a compromise between individual and society.

quotes.quote: This mask, i.e., the ad hoc adopted attitude, I have called the persona,79 which was the name for the masks worn by actors in antiquity.

a complicated system of relations between the individual consciousness and society, fittingly enough a kind of mask, designed on the one hand to make a definite impression upon others, and, on the other, to conceal the true nature of the individual
Fundamentally the persona is nothing real: it is a compromise between individual and society as to what a man should appear to be.

sections.title: Its function
sections.line: CW6 ¶801: Jung's definition of the persona as a functional complex concerned with the relation to objects.

quotes.quote: a functional complex that comes into existence for reasons of adaptation or personal convenience, but is by no means identical with the individuality. The persona is exclusively concerned with the relation to objects

sections.title: The collective's mask
sections.line: CW7 ¶465 (the mask worn by the collective psyche) and CW18 ¶1334 (the persona as a composite of the individual's behaviour and the role attributed to him by the public).

quotes.quote: It is, as its name implies, only the mask worn by the collective psyche, a mask that feigns individuality
The persona is never the true character; it is a composite of the individual's behaviour and of the role attributed to him by the public

sections.title: Taking it off
sections.line: CW7 ¶505: the dissolution of the persona as an indispensable condition for individuation, and what Jung says of conscious intention; CW6 ¶807: what he says follows for anyone who is himself his outward role.

quotes.quote: The dissolution of the persona is therefore an indispensable condition for individuation. It is, however, impossible to achieve individuation by conscious intention
Anyone who is himself his outward role will infallibly succumb to the inner processes
